concept.idea: A perimeter witness clamped to the chain-link at the property's edge — past the WiFi, past mains power. It would feel the fence's own vibration signature (climb, cut, rattle), debounce it into the same small signed claims every Canary speaks, and carry them home over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, solar-fed, with the relay pod as its first hop.

points.v: clamped to chain-link in a shaded run — panel in the sun, cell in the shade; lithium ages in heat and must not charge below freezing.
Ed25519-signed fence-event claims over the mesh, hash-chained — and Meshtastic's position broadcast stays off: a perimeter node must not map the perimeter.
solar over battery via an external charge controller (the kit's onboard charger is a slow ~50-100 mA and has no solar input); target is multi-day overcast survival.
the kit ships with no IP rating — the sealed clamp enclosure, with the antenna stood off the fence's metal plane, is ours to design and print-validate.

radio.v: Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 + Wio-SX1262 (SKU 102010611, $9.90) — same XIAO family as every Canary host; Meshtastic pre-flashed since Oct 2024
Semtech SX1262 · 862-930 MHz, one hardware for EU868/US915 (region set in firmware) · up to +22 dBm · U.FL antenna
ESP32-S3R8 dual-core 240 MHz · 8 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM · WiFi b/g/n + BLE 5.0 · 21 x 17.8 mm
mainline target seeed-xiao-s3 (HW_MODEL 81), community-supported tier, web-flasher entry 'Seeed XIAO S3'
LIS3DH accelerometer natively supported on the free I2C bus; the Detection Sensor module reads a vibration switch on a free GPIO - a zero-custom-code Phase 0 exists
~130 mA measured as an always-on node (community, single-source) vs ~11.7 mA idle on the nRF52840 sibling kit - an ~11x gap the field mule must adjudicate
2-5 km typical; >2.5 km measured by Seeed on the 2 dBi antenna (open-terrain 20 km+ claims are marketing)

plan: Phase 0, zero custom firmware: stock Meshtastic + LIS3DH on I2C + a vibration switch on a free GPIO (Detection Sensor module) — a field mule on a real fence, measuring false alarms and the solar budget through weather.
Let the mule's power data adjudicate ESP32-S3 vs the nRF52840 sibling kit (~11x idle gap; the S3 buys WiFi and price, the nRF52 buys the battery).
Close the platform question: Meshtastic module on stock firmware vs the native witness stack with a mesh transport.
Then the witness surface: v1 fence canonical, Ed25519 chain, health claims — the same trust rules as the rest of the fleet, position broadcast off forever.
Enclosure last, informed by the mule: chain-link clamp, antenna stood off the metal plane, IP-rated, printed and validated like every other Canary shell.

devices.name: Canary Guardian
devices.tagline: A witness you wear — press and hold and your people hear you, off-grid, no cell, no one else can see where you've been. Coming soon.
devices.board: XIAO nRF52840 + Wio-SX1262 (Meshtastic) — the low-power sibling of the Fence Guard kit

network.mdns: none — a worn node lives past the WiFi by design
network.mqtt: via mesh gateway (concept): duress_asserted + heartbeat/zone claims, signed chain

devices.status: coming soon — concept, research staged

concept.idea: A small, screenless LoRa node you *choose to wear*, asleep almost always. Press and hold and it signs a coarse 'I need help' claim and shouts it to your own people over the mesh; a quiet periodic 'I'm OK' heartbeat means its silence can raise the alarm on its own. It is the deliberate inverse of a tracking tag — it answers 'is this person alright?', asked only by the wearer, and is architecturally incapable of saying where they've been.

points.v: the wearer, and only the wearer — they arm it, press it, and silence it; no one can turn it on from afar. A witness someone else controls is surveillance.
an Ed25519-signed duress or heartbeat claim over the mesh, coarse zone + coarse time — never a location stream, never audio, never a fine coordinate. GPS (if ever fitted) ships off.

a best-effort off-grid shout your people can hear, not a 911-grade guarantee — Meshtastic is ~1-3 s, retried, but not assured delivery. A BLE-to-phone fallback relays over cell when a paired phone is near.

points.k: Falls are a prompt, not a claim
points.v: real-world accelerometer fall detection runs ~57% sensitivity with up to dozens of false alarms a day; a suspected impact starts an 'are you OK?' countdown the wearer can cancel — it never writes an unqualified 'fall' into the sealed log.

radio.v: Seeed XIAO nRF52840 + Wio-SX1262 Kit — the pin-incompatible low-power sibling of Fence Guard's ESP32-S3 kit; Meshtastic firmware family

the T-Echo (nRF52840) gets days of standby on 850 mAh where an ESP32 node on a bigger 2600 mAh cell lasts ~a day; nRF52 sleeps at single-digit uA vs the ESP32-S3's real ~14 uA+ — a worn safety device can't be a daily-charge device
Semtech SX1262 · 862-930 MHz, one hardware for EU868/US915 (region set in firmware) · up to +22 dBm · U.FL antenna
TX-mostly, deep-sleep by default — ~150-300 uA average gives weeks on a 500 mAh LiPo; continuous LoRa RX would collapse that to ~1 day/100 mAh, so RX is event-gated
a body-worn antenna underperforms bench figures — a few hundred m to ~1-2 km urban, 3-5 km suburban; lean on fixed fleet relays (home Canaries, a Fence Guard) to catch the shout

plan: Phase 0, zero custom firmware: stock Meshtastic + the Detection Sensor Module on a button GPIO — a real press-and-hold duress burst on the nRF52840 kit, worn, measuring range-near-flesh and battery through real days.
Add the one new claim kind the flagship needs, duress_asserted, across the dictionary + both HA mirrors under the drift-linter; heartbeat stays absence-inferred (no new kind).
Define the BLE-to-phone fallback — the honest belt-and-braces for a best-effort mesh.
Then the check-in path: RTC heartbeat, coarse battery field so 'low battery' never reads as 'wearer down', and the IMU wired only as an 'are you OK?' prompt.
Coarse zone presence last, via anchor proximity — entered/left events, never a coordinate; settle its claim mapping then.
Enclosure: a screenless pendant/pocket puck, self-announcing (visible/haptic 'I'm on') — the anti-AirTag, printed and validated like every other Canary shell.

devices.tagline: Watches the open approach — 'a large mover is coming up the drive' — camera-free, months on a battery, over the mesh. Coming soon.
devices.board: XIAO ESP32-S3 + low-power Doppler radar (I/Q) + Wio-SX1262 (Meshtastic)
senses: Doppler motion + radial speed (concept)
approaching vs receding direction, needs an I/Q part (concept)

network.mdns: none — the approach is past the WiFi by design
network.mqtt: via mesh gateway (concept): coarse mover/direction claims, signed chain

devices.status: coming soon — concept, research staged

concept.idea: A cheap, camera-free radar node that watches an open approach — a driveway, a gate, a yard, a trail — sips microwatts so it runs for months on a battery or forever on a little solar, and reports coarse 'something's moving, this way, roughly this big' claims to the mesh. Drawn from studying Samraksh's BumbleBee Doppler mote: it replicates the CIVILIAN 'virtual fence' capability (motion + direction + coarse class, off-grid, low power) and hard-stops the MILITARY half (tracking, per-target IDs, gait identity) that the same sensing was funded to do. It's the motion counterpart to Fence Guard's vibration and the low-power outdoor sibling of Canary Sense's rich indoor radar.

points.k: Why it's more than a PIR
points.v: Doppler reads DIRECTION (a car arriving vs leaving, someone walking up the path vs away) and ignores the thermal ghosts — sun on pavement, an HVAC plume — that plague PIR; it works through darkness, light foliage and rain where a camera is blinded or would feel creepy.

it says 'a LARGE mover is approaching zone X' (a physical predicate) and never who, never a path, never a per-target ID or gait signature. Coarse class is a fact about your property; a track or an identity is surveillance of a person — it inherits Canary Sense's §2.2 privacy contract wholesale.

our 60 GHz FMCW radar (Sense) is a better sensor indoors in every way EXCEPT power — it can't live on a fencepost for a season. A pulsed low-GHz Doppler front-end can. Ranger is the tier Sense's power budget can't reach, not a downgrade of it.

a single-channel HB100/CDM324 gives motion + speed but not the sign of the Doppler shift; approaching-vs-receding needs a quadrature (two-IF) part like the InnoSenT IPM-165 — the true BumbleBee analog. Budget it if direction matters.

radio.v: commodity Doppler: HB100 (10.525 GHz, ~2 mA at 5% pulse duty, 2-16 m) or CDM324 (24 GHz) for motion-only; InnoSenT IPM-165-class I/Q part for approach/recede direction; all far cheaper and lower-power than an FMCW chip
Seeed MR24HPC1 (24 GHz FMCW 'human static presence Lite') adds still-presence + distance at the perimeter — a cheaper cousin of Sense, if you want presence-while-motionless outdoors

XIAO ESP32-S3 amplifies the radar IF into its ADC and runs a windowed FFT for speed/direction/coarse-class on-device (BumbleBee did displacement detection on a tiny FPGA; the S3 + ADC is comfortably enough for coarse Doppler features)
same XIAO + Wio-SX1262 Meshtastic kit as Fence Guard (SKU 102010611); coarse claims leave as an Ed25519-signed chain over LoRa, position broadcast off — a virtual fence must not map the fence

the whole point of the tier: pulse/duty-cycle the front-end (avoid 30-40 mA continuous-wave) + ESP32 asleep between looks -> uW-mW average -> months on a LiPo, indefinite on small solar with Fence Guard's charge-controller guidance

sources.name: NSF 'Virtual Fences for Sustainable Protection' (the civilian grant)
HB100 / CDM324 / RCWL-0516 Doppler part comparison
Seeed MR24HPC1 24 GHz FMCW module (richer-tier alt)

plan: Phase 0, cheap and coarse: an HB100/CDM324 IF into the XIAO ESP32-S3 ADC + a windowed FFT + stock Meshtastic -> a real battery/solar approach witness emitting large-vs-small-mover claims, measuring the outdoor false-alarm floor (wind-blown branch vs deer vs person vs car).
Add direction with an I/Q (IPM-165-class) part; decide how approaching/receding is represented (a claim attribute vs a new approach_detected kind).
Reuse boundary_crossing_object_large/_small for the coarse type claims; keep walk/run/crawl activity as a local dashboard hint, never a sealed claim.
Parallel, hardware-free: apply the same micro-Doppler classifier to Canary Sense's existing 60 GHz radar for an indoor coarse-class claim (§6) — the 'do it with what we have' win.
Enclosure: a weatherproof radome (radar sees through plastic, not metal) aimed along the approach; reuse Fence Guard's solar/antenna-standoff guidance, printed and validated like every Canary shell.

devices.name: Canary Feeder
devices.tagline: A solar bird-feeder cam that wakes when a bird lands, decides 'a bird visited' on-device, and never ships raw video. Coming soon.
devices.board: XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense (+ optional Grove Vision AI V2 NPU); perch break-beam/load-cell trigger; solar
senses: on-device bird-vs-not + coarse species bucket (concept)
perch landing via break-beam or load cell (concept)
a bird visit as a small-object claim, snapshot local-only (concept)

network.mqtt: SmallObjectBoundaryCrossing claim + signed chain; snapshot stays local, never sealed

devices.status: coming soon — concept, research staged

concept.idea: A solar-powered camera on your feeder that wakes when a bird actually lands (a perch break-beam or load cell, ~0 mA until triggered — not a twitchy PIR), confirms 'a bird visited' with a tiny on-device model, seals that as a coarse small-object claim, keeps a snapshot LOCALLY for your delight, and never ships raw video anywhere. A Vision-family device: on-device inference in, coarse claim out.

points.k: Why a perch trigger, not PIR
points.v: a small bird is a marginal thermal target, PIR false-fires on sun/wind and CAN'T see through the camera's glass (needs its own HDPE window); a break-beam/load-cell on the fixed landing point is weather-immune and near-zero false-wakes — and false wakes are a power-survival bug on a solar node.

'10,000 species' is a CLOUD claim (Bird Buddy uploads video). On a ~$15 ESP32-S3 node, 'a bird is present' is reliable and coarse buckets (songbird/dove/corvid/squirrel) work with a locally-trimmed dataset. So the sealed claim is 'a bird visited (coarse bucket)' — the achievable and privacy-right thing.

the most misunderstood point: LiFePO4 does NOT solve cold charging (it's stricter). Its win is cycle life + cold DISCHARGE. Size for 5-10 days autonomy with a low-temp-cutoff BMS; autonomy, not chemistry, carries you through a freeze.

points.k: A sealed box fogs the lens
points.v: full sealing traps humid air and fogs the lens at dawn — use a breathable Gore vent + rechargeable desiccant, a hydrophobic lens coating and a short hood, camera aimed slightly down so water runs off.

radio.v: perch break-beam or load cell (HX711) — the bird's landing IS the wake, ~0 mA idle, immune to sun/snow/wind/cold; camera confirms via FOMO. Skip RCWL/HB100 radar here (5-8 m over-range, metal-feeder false triggers)

XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense (Edge Impulse FOMO, bird-vs-not + a few buckets, ~$14) or step up to Grove Vision AI V2 (Himax + Ethos-U55 NPU, dependable buckets at ~0.35 W, ~$49); reCamera is Linux-class idle power, not a sleep/wake node

LiFePO4 ~6-10 Wh + low-temp-charge-cutoff BMS; oversize the panel to 5-10 W (STC) tilted ~60 deg for weak winter sun + snow-shedding; optional supercap to buffer the ~250 mA wake pulses when the cold battery is current-limited
sleep-dominated: ~1-5 mA deep sleep (camera rail OFF), ~160-300 mA for 1-3 s per wake -> ~0.5-1 Wh/day; killing false wakes matters more than shaving inference time
IP66/67 box + Gore vent + desiccant (assembled dry), hydrophobic cover glass + printed hood, downward tilt; electronics/battery in the insulated feeder base

sources.name: Edge Impulse — Grove Vision AI V2 on-device object detection
Security Today — camera condensation / breathable vent beats sealed

plan: Phase 0: a perch break-beam/load-cell wake + XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense FOMO 'bird-vs-not' + the existing webhook claim path — a real feeder node on the bench, measuring false-wake rate and capture power.
Train coarse local-species buckets on a trimmed regional dataset (not a universal model); map the bucket to a SmallObjectBoundaryCrossing attribute.
Local-only snapshot for the owner's delight (never sealed, never uploaded) — same posture as Vision's local preview.
Winter power hardening: LiFePO4 + low-temp-cutoff BMS + oversized tilted panel + autonomy sizing; optional supercap pulse buffer.
Enclosure: a printed feeder body with an integrated break-beam/load-cell perch, Gore vent + desiccant, hydrophobic hooded lens — printed and validated like every Canary shell.

concept.idea: A weight platform under a STANDARD litter box (the Purina Petivity pattern) that quietly learns each cat's body weight and bathroom pattern from a load-cell stream, and — as opt-in, non-diagnostic wellbeing signals, never a camera — surfaces the changes vets treat as early warnings, including the one that's a genuine emergency. The honest claim is 'we surface changes worth asking your vet about', never 'we detect kidney disease'.

points.v: Purina Petivity's litter-box data trained a peer-reviewed model that flags CKD at ~90% F1 (Quimby et al., Ohio State). Body-weight-trend down -> CKD/diabetes/hyperthyroid; up frequency + volume -> polyuria; MANY short straining visits with ~zero output -> urinary blockage, a life-threatening emergency mostly in male cats (24-48 h).

points.k: Size the load cell to the load
points.v: the HX711 gives ~+/-0.1% of full scale, so a 4x50 kg (200 kg) array is +/-200 g — too coarse for a 30-100 g clump. A single 5-10 kg bar (~+/-5-10 g) suits a small box; recover the body-weight TREND with heavy plateau averaging + a multi-day rolling median.

points.k: Drift is the real enemy, not resolution
points.v: load cells drift with temperature and creep; continuous AUTO-TARE (re-baseline when flat and no visit) absorbs litter scatter, scooping, refills and evaporation, and a big-refill re-baseline stops a top-up logging as a giant 'deposit'.

points.k: Health data never touches the sealed log
points.v: weight/frequency/duration ride the wellbeing channel exactly like Canary Sense's vitals: non-diagnostic, P1 opt-in, HA-only, never sealed-logged. The descriptor allowlist makes it structurally impossible for a health number to seal an event. Multi-cat by weight (or an owned RFID tag) — never a camera.

radio.v: load cell(s) + HX711 24-bit ADC under a standard box -> body weight (plateau minus tare), per-visit deposit (baseline delta), visit detection (step edges); trimmed-median over the plateau because a moving cat is the dominant noise source
a single VL53L1X ToF at the entrance for crisp entry/exit duration + the paws-on-rim half-step-in case; a $1 PIR is the budget fallback

weight-based clustering (free, reliable when cats differ by >~0.5 kg; blurs for same-weight cats) with an optional opt-in RFID/BLE collar tag + entrance reader as the certainty upgrade — the same you-own-the-tag posture as the rest of the fleet

two-point calibration at install stored in NVS; continuous auto-tare; visit segmentation with a min-weight + min-duration gate to reject paw-on-rim; report body weight as a multi-day rolling median where the clinical value lives

concept.idea: A cheap, weatherproof, camera-free sensor that knows when your dog is at the door WAITING to come in (not merely passing), in all weather. No single cheap sensor does this reliably, so it ships as two honest tiers: a trained IP65 paw-button (a switch closes = a ContactStateChange claim), and a 24 GHz FMCW radar behind a radome with a zone + dwell rule (PresenceInRestrictedZone). Pick the tier, or hybridize for the strongest result.

points.v: (1) detecting a dog through snow/sun/cold — only RF (radar / owned tag) is weather-immune; PIR, mats, capacitive and break-beams all fail. (2) 'waiting' vs 'passing' — a zone+dwell+identity problem only FMCW radar (position+persistence) or a collar tag (identity+proximity) can express.

points.k: Tier 1: the trained paw-button (cheapest, most reliable)
points.v: an IP65 waterproof button with a SELF-POWERED RF activator: near-zero false alarms (only a deliberate press), literally a ContactStateChange claim. Costs: you must train the dog, and the button can snow-bury/ice (mount sheltered and angled; add a radar backstop).

points.k: Tier 2: FMCW radar, and it MUST be FMCW not Doppler
points.v: a waiting dog is nearly still, so cheap Doppler (RCWL/HB100 — the Ranger tier) goes blind exactly when needed; FMCW (HLK-LD2410/LD2450) senses a still target + gives position. 'Waiting not passing' = target in a ~0.5 m zone AND velocity ~0 AND dwell >= N seconds. Behind a radome, RF sees through iced-over plastic.

single-radar dog-vs-person is THE classification that fails (~90% only with 4 radars). Mitigate by aiming the sensed slab knee-height (a standing adult's torso falls outside it) and/or adding an OWNED collar tag for identity — never pretend radar tells a dog from a bending person on its own.

radio.v: trained IP65 paw/nose button (Mighty Paw ~$30 or generic $13-18), self-powered RF fob activator, door-side XIAO receiver turns the press into a signed ContactStateChange

HLK-LD2410 (~$4-9) or LD2450 (X/Y + speed for up to 3 targets, ~$10-15) sealed in an IP67 enclosure that doubles as a low-loss radome (polycarbonate ~2.3 mm class); ESPHome-style zone/dwell logic on a XIAO
an OWNED BLE collar tag + door anchor confirms 'it's our dog, within 1 m' and inherently rejects people/cats/clutter (no tag); IP67-potted, CR2032 lasts months but sags in deep cold

PIR (no contrast vs snow, can't see through glass, can't hold 'still waiting'); pressure mat (snow burial); capacitive (rain bridges it); break-beam (a crossing = passing, not waiting); Doppler radar (blind to a still dog)

storm clutter drops radar detection 10-30% (CFAR + trajectory + dwell suppress, not eliminate); a thick wet-snow slab still degrades the radome; button/tag cold-battery sag — the honest reason the tiers back each other up

sources.name: Mighty Paw Smart Bell (trained waterproof dog doorbell)
HLK-LD2450 FMCW radar (X/Y + speed, ESPHome zones)
TI — radar radome design (RF through plastic/glass)

plan: Phase 0 (cheapest): a trained IP65 paw-button + a door-side XIAO receiver -> a signed ContactStateChange claim. Real, near-zero-false-alarm, needs only dog training.
Tier 2: an LD2450 behind a printed radome with a zone + velocity~0 + dwell>=N rule for 'waiting not passing'; tune the knee-height geometry on a real door and dog.
Add the optional owned BLE collar tag for identity confirmation (rejects people/cats/clutter; confirms our dog).
Hybrid: button primary + radar backstop for snow-buried-button days; or radar+tag for the no-training install.
Enclosure: an IP67 radome door mount (sheltered, angled) reusing Ranger's radome and Fence Guard's cold-battery guidance; printed and validated.

concept.idea: A small node that watches a room's temperature, humidity, and air quality — and whether it still has power — and pokes your phone when the room leaves your pet's safe band, the air turns smoky or stuffy, the HVAC seems to have failed, or the power goes out. Folds pet temp/thermostat, air quality, and power-outage alerting into one environmental node, because they share sensors, thresholds, and the same remote-alert relay.

points.k: Detect HVAC FAILURE, not just a threshold
points.v: a fixed threshold is slow. Watch rate-of-change — temp rising when the AC should cool, or falling in winter past a slope — to catch a furnace/AC (or power) failure minutes early; species/zone safe bands, not one number (a cold-blooded pet in a failed vivarium heater is a fast emergency).

integrate AirGradient now (open HW+FW, local HTTP API + MQTT, zero new firmware) -> build our own XIAO + Sensirion SEN5x + SCD41 node later. Wildfire-smoke PM2.5 (a rate-of-change spike) is the killer use case; first alert at EPA AQI 101 (PM2.5 > 35.4).

points.k: Two honesty rules the design encodes
points.v: eCO2 is NOT CO2 (it's a VOC-derived guess — use true NDIR for CO2); and CO is NOT CO2 (carbon monoxide is a separate, acute killer needing a dedicated life-safety alarm). The '1000 ppm CO2 = unhealthy' line is a retired ASHRAE myth — CO2 is a ventilation proxy, framed 'ventilate', never 'danger'.

points.k: The outage is the same design problem
points.v: losing power is the alert whose transport must survive losing power. Detect it by ABSENCE (heartbeat silence, not a heroic last gasp) and carry the poke out over LoRa/Meshtastic to an independently-powered gateway, because WiFi/internet die too. Payoff for pets: power out -> HVAC dead -> you're told while you can still act.

radio.v: Sensirion SHT4x (or BME280 for pressure) — accurate, cheap, low-power; away from self-heating parts
Sensirion SEN5x (PM1/2.5/10 + VOC/NOx index + T/RH in one) + SCD41 true NDIR CO2; CO stays a separate dedicated life-safety sensor, never conflated with CO2
an off-the-shelf AirGradient ONE via GET /measures/current or its native MQTT (mqttBrokerUrl) -> our adapter maps JSON to wellbeing signals + threshold alerts; no cloud, no fork
opto/mains-present input + a mains-node heartbeat; a battery/solar/mesh peer infers the outage from silence; a supercap last-gasp is a best-effort bonus, never trusted
EPA AQI 101 (PM2.5 > 35.4) first alert + a wildfire-smoke rate-of-change spike; CO2 > ~1000 ppm 'ventilate', > ~1400 'poorly ventilated'; WHO 2021 (annual 5, 24h 15) for the healthy-air framing

sources.name: ASHRAE indoor-CO2 position (the retired 1000 ppm myth)

plan: Phase 0: XIAO + SHT4x + a mains-present input -> temp/humidity wellbeing signals + safe-band + rate-of-change HVAC-failure alerts through the alert relay.
Air quality v1: integrate an AirGradient node via local API/MQTT; map PM2.5/CO2/VOC to wellbeing signals + EPA-AQI/CO2 threshold alerts (eCO2 and CO kept honest/separate).
Outage: mains-node heartbeat + absence-inference on a battery/mesh peer; carry the poke over Meshtastic to a powered gateway; supercap last-gasp as a bonus.
Air quality v2 (never-rot): our own XIAO + SEN5x + SCD41 node signing claims on-device.
Tune safe-band defaults per species and the HVAC/ smoke-spike slopes on real rooms; seed golden vectors.

concept.idea: A low-resolution thermal sensor under the range hood that notices when a burner's been left hot and unattended — the leading cause of home fires — and a microphone that relays your existing smoke/CO alarm to your phone while you're out. Camera-free, alert-only. It is an AWARENESS AID, explicitly not a fire detector, not a substitute for UL smoke/CO alarms, and not an auto-shutoff.

points.k: The value is unattended cooking, not flames
points.v: cooking is the #1 cause of home fires and unattended cooking is by far the leading ignition factor (~a third; NFPA ~172,900 fires/yr). So the hero detection is 'a hot cooktop persisting with NO motion in the room for N minutes' — thermal + presence fusion, not flame spectroscopy.

the hero is a 32x24 thermal array reading to +300 C (a pan runs 150-250 C, a dry pan 300 C+). The cheaper AMG8833 (8x8) saturates at 80 C and can't tell a simmer from a scorching dry pan — disqualifying. 768 pixels is witness-grade (no faces, no text): a sensor, not a camera.

points.k: Relay your existing alarm (the clever cheap add)
points.v: a mic that matches the standardized T3 (fire) / T4 (CO) alarm cadence — not loudness — turns any UL alarm you own into a remote 'we heard your alarm' notification. Maps to the existing AcousticImpulseInZone claim; real prior art (FireAvert, ESPHome listeners).

we have no actuator, so we're alert-only (the Wallflower lane), NOT the EN 50615 prevention lane. It does not replace UL smoke/CO alarms or an auto-shutoff, cannot suppress or shut off a fire, and may miss or false-alarm. We skip flame sensors (a flame != a hazard on gas, blind on electric/induction) and don't claim gas-leak detection.

radio.v: Melexis MLX90640 32x24 thermal IR array (-40..+300 C), mounted under the hood looking down, ~2-4 Hz; detects per-burner hot/on, dry-pan scorch (runaway temp on low thermal mass), flare (hot-area growth), boil-over (hot region spreading past the pot footprint)

a PIR or a reused kitchen Canary Sense radar -> 'hot cooktop + no human motion for N minutes' = the unattended-cooking alert, mirroring how Innohome/Inirv define hazard (minus their auto-shutoff — we have no actuator)
an I2S/analog mic + a temporal-cadence matcher for the ISO 8201 / NFPA 72 T3 (three pulses) and T4 (four pulses) patterns at ~3-4 kHz; match cadence not loudness to reject kitchen clatter

thermal frames processed on-device, only the derived coarse claim leaves; no camera, no video. Gas leak (unlit gas) needs a proper catalytic/NDIR sensor and is explicitly out of scope; CO stays your dedicated alarm's job

concept.idea: A coin-sized node you stick on the washer or dryer (or any machine that shakes while it works) that knows — purely from vibration — when the cycle is running and, more usefully, when it's done, and pokes your phone so the laundry doesn't sit and sour. No electrical work, no smart plug, no per-appliance wiring: an accelerometer on the shell, and 'done' inferred from stillness.

points.v: a washer/dryer vibrates while running and goes still when done. A stick-on accelerometer works on any brand, gas or electric, with no electrical access — cheaper and simpler than a smart plug, CT clamp, or a brand-specific end-of-cycle-beep listener.

running = sustained vibration above a learned floor; done = vibration ceasing for N minutes — the same presence-via-active-signal / absence-via-timeout pattern used for Car Mode, Guardian, the meshtastic adapter and the power-outage witness. Robust, no coupling to the machine's electronics.

the sensor is an LIS3DH accelerometer on I2C with a hardware motion/vibration interrupt so the MCU deep-sleeps and wakes only when the machine shakes — the exact part Fence Guard specs, ~$1-2, adhesive-mount, months on a small battery.

points.k: A convenience witness, not a safety device
points.v: on-device processing emits only the coarse state, never a raw motion trace; it senses a MACHINE's vibration, nothing about people. It won't catch a leak or an overheat — it's 'your laundry's done / your washer's walking', delivered through the alert relay.

radio.v: LIS3DH (or MPU-class) accelerometer, hardware vibration-wake interrupt -> deep-sleep until the machine shakes; a brief auto-learn of the idle floor and running band on first use (machines vibrate differently)
sustained-vibration = running (short debounce rejects a door slam / passing truck); ceasing-for-N-minutes = done; an off-rhythm spike = optional unbalanced-load 'walking' nudge

smart plug/CT clamp needs electrical access (240 V dryer circuits, panel); a contact sensor tells door state not cycle-done; an end-of-cycle-beep listener is brand-specific and easily masked — vibration is the stick-on universal
'done' reports shortly after the machine stops (the absence timeout, a couple of minutes), not the instant — because instant-stop is exactly the unreliable signal we avoid elsewhere

Auto-learn the idle floor + running band on first use so it adapts to any machine.

points.v: even a $1,999 purpose-built underwater camera (Coral Manta) only claims 'unmoving body underwater ~15 s' and still won't call itself a substitute for supervision. the defining scenario is a child wandering out at night/dawn while adults sleep — when supervision is weakest and an alert is worth the most. Vision Pro's starlight low-light sensing is the single most important capability; a daytime-only camera is blind exactly then.

concept.idea: A solar sensor at the yard/street boundary that watches a VIRTUAL PLANE at the curb and warns a nearby adult when a small child appears to be crossing TOWARD the road — one extra set of eyes, never a fence. points.v: even DOT-funded roadside animal-detection ran >90% false positives in the field (desensitizing the people meant to react) and ~40% downtime in a snowstorm; operators found it 'impossible to eliminate false triggers while still guaranteeing large animals are detected'. The hard part is classifying the right target and rejecting everything else, in weather, cheaply — only partly solved by professionals.

points.k: A directional boundary-plane crossing, not motion
points.v: a virtual plane at the curb, gated on crossing TOWARD the road (the line-crossing/tripwire analytic with direction) — this removes the biggest confound: walking along the sidewalk or playing safely in the yard. Only toward-street crossings count.

points.k: Fusion: radar triggers, starlight camera confirms
points.v: radar (24/60 GHz FMCW) is the weather-immune always-on direction+dwell trigger but can't classify a child; a toward-street event wakes a Vision Pro starlight camera to confirm child-class and reject cars/adults/pets. Vision is worst at exactly the child class, so it must be the confirmation layer, not the trigger; radar-wakes-camera also fits the solar budget.

points.k: Children are the hardest class to detect
points.v: detectors miss children ~20%+ more than adults (small bounding boxes, erratic movement, adult-biased training data). So size is a BIAS toward alerting, never a suppression gate — you cannot maximize child sensitivity AND minimize false alarms, so we bias to sensitivity and accept nuisance alerts. A 'zero false alarms' tuning is one that will one day stay silent for a real child.

radio.v: low-power 24/60 GHz FMCW radar: range + radial velocity (toward/away) + dwell, immune to fog/rain/snow/dark/blowing-leaves; defines the boundary zone and fires only on toward-street crossings

AND four weak signals: directional crossing of the curb plane + zone geometry excluding sidewalk-parallel/in-yard + small-size/low-height bias + dwell/track persistence (kills leaves, rain streaks, single-frame blips)

no lithium charges below 0 C -> LiFePO4 + low-temp-cutoff BMS, sized for winter worst-case with multi-day autonomy; duty-cycle (radar awake, camera only on a boundary event) keeps the winter budget feasible - the shared Fence Guard/Ranger rule

points.v: an LIS3DH on the gate leaf (the Fence Guard part) reads the resting TILT (open-vs-closed as an angle) and the swing (motion) on a wake-on-motion interrupt, sleeping at ~single-uA between events. One self-contained unit, open-ANGLE not just open/closed, and a rattle/climb/shove is a distinct vibration signature (Fence Guard's trick) — a security bonus for free.

points.k: Reed switch = the dead-simple cheapest binary
points.v: a magnet on the gate + a sealed reed on the post: truly ~0 uA quiescent, unambiguous open/closed, ~$1, weatherproof commodity. Trade-offs: two ALIGNED parts, the gap must stay in range, and it can't tell angle or sense a climb. Both map to the existing ContactStateChange claim — no new vocabulary.

points.k: Super low power: a primary cell often beats solar
points.v: at a few wake-on-interrupt events a day, a primary lithium cell (CR2032, or LiSOCl2 for the cold) runs for YEARS and sidesteps the cold-battery problem entirely — since it's never charged, the 'no lithium charges below 0 C' rule that bites every rechargeable simply doesn't apply. Solar + a small LiFePO4 is the 'never touch it' option, but for a cold gate a multi-year primary cell is often simpler.

opened/closed (ContactStateChange); LEFT OPEN too long (absence-inference: no 'closed' within N minutes -> a 'gate still open' nag, the Car Mode/Guardian/Chore pattern); and rattled/climbed (a tamper signal, TamperDetected). All processed on-device to a coarse state; only the state/alert leaves.

concept.idea: A small IMU + LoRa node that lives in your parked car and witnesses the states you're NOT present for: 'someone moved my car' (theft/tow) and 'where did I last leave it' (off-grid find-my-car). It supersedes Car Mode, which sensed the one state that barely matters — the car running, with you in it — and drew power from the ignition-USB port that's dead exactly when a parked-car witness would need it. Value comes entirely from the node's own IMU and a long-range radio, never from tapping the car.

points.v: Car Mode announced 'I have power → the car is here'; but theft, tows and break-ins happen parked and owner-away, when ignition-USB is dead. A parked-car witness runs on always-hot or battery power and watches for MOTION, not power.

concept.request_body:
Seen the Vehicle Guard concept card. What I'd want from a parked-car witness:

- theft/tow alert, find-my-car, or both:
- always-hot fuse tap or internal battery:
- is there a home/neighbor mesh to hear it park:
- any interest in the cabin thermometer (temp only, not occupancy):

persona.name: Watchman the Wheel Warden
persona.shape: sturdy little canary curled up asleep on a tiny wheel chock, one eye cracked open, a faint radio ring above
persona.story: Watchman naps in the parked car all day and does nothing at all — until the car moves without you, and then it sends one quiet signed word to your people over the mesh. It refuses to read the car's secrets or map where you go; it only knows 'still' from 'moved' and 'here' from 'gone'. Watchman wears a concept ribbon because honest products say what is real — and because it would rather guard a still car than pretend to guard a moving one.
good_for: Theft and tow alerts when the car is off-grid and you're away
Finding a car parked past cell coverage
A vehicle witness that never taps the bus or maps your trips
persona.catchphrase: I sleep in a still car and wake for a moving one.

devices.name: Canary Vehicle
devices.tagline: Reads your car's own ignition state, passively — never writes to the bus, never learns where you've been.
devices.board: Linux SBC (e.g. Raspberry Pi) + MCP2515 CAN HAT, SocketCAN
senses: vehicle CAN bus (passive, read-only)

network.mdns: none — runs adapter_host, not a flashed Canary firmware host
network.mqtt: via the can_bus sensor adapter: vehicle_arrival_departure claims + signed chain

devices.status: adapter shipped & unit-tested (src/adapter/can_bus.rs, edge-triggered, 11 tests) — vehicle-specific signal profiles documented but not bench-confirmed against a real car

persona.name: Hush the Wire Listener
persona.shape: a low, alert canary with a single coiled antenna-whisker and folded, listening-only wings — no beak wide enough to speak
persona.story: Hush was built with no voice on purpose. It rides quietly on your car's own wire, hears the ignition switch the way every other module in the car already does, and says only ever one thing outward: here, or gone. Hush never asks the car a question, never sends it a command, and never once remembers where the car has been — only whether it's home.
good_for: Telling the household fleet when a car arrives or leaves, without a phone geofence
Households with a small always-on Linux hub (a Pi) willing to ride along in the vehicle
Proving, structurally, that a witness can listen to a car without ever tracking it
persona.catchphrase: I only ever answer one question: are you home?
